input: Find bribery and corruption enforcement involving Ericsson, including its deferred prosecution agreement

events.type: FCPA criminal bribery/corruption enforcement; deferred prosecution agreement
events.jurisdiction: United States — Southern District of New York
events.status: settled (DPA); Ericsson Egypt Ltd pleaded guilty
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson; Ericsson Egypt Ltd; U.S. Department of Justice/SDNY and IRS Criminal Investigation
events.amount: US$520,650,432 criminal penalty, including a US$9,520,000 fine paid on behalf of Ericsson Egypt
events.summary: Ericsson entered a DPA and admitted participating in conspiracies involving bribes, slush funds, sham contracts, false invoices, books-and-records violations and inadequate controls in Djibouti, China, Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait; Ericsson Egypt pleaded guilty to an anti-bribery conspiracy.

events.type: SEC FCPA civil enforcement — bribery, books and records and internal controls
events.jurisdiction: United States — Securities and Exchange Commission
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson and Ericsson subsidiaries; U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
events.amount: US$539,920,000 disgorgement of profits and prejudgment interest; more than US$1 billion combined with the DOJ criminal resolution
events.summary: The SEC charged Ericsson over a large-scale bribery scheme using sham consultants and alleged that subsidiaries obtained approximately US$427 million of business through third-party bribes in Saudi Arabia, China and Djibouti, with related FCPA misconduct in Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait.

events.type: DPA-breach determination and Iraq-related corruption investigation
events.jurisdiction: United States — U.S. Department of Justice
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson; U.S. Department of Justice
events.summary: The DOJ informed Ericsson that it had provided insufficient information before entering the DPA about its 2019 Iraq internal investigation and had breached the DPA by failing to inform DOJ about that investigation after entering the DPA; Ericsson's later filing said the Iraq-related matters remained under DOJ investigation.

events.type: FCPA criminal enforcement — breach of deferred prosecution agreement and guilty plea
events.jurisdiction: United States — Southern District of New York
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson; U.S. Department of Justice/SDNY and IRS Criminal Investigation
events.summary: After finding that Ericsson failed to truthfully disclose evidence concerning the Djibouti and China schemes and failed promptly to disclose Iraq-related misconduct, DOJ required Ericsson to plead guilty to the two charges deferred by the 2019 DPA, serve probation through June 2024 and accept a one-year extension of the independent compliance monitor.

events.jurisdiction: United States — Securities and Exchange Commission
events.status: investigated; SEC Staff said it did not intend to recommend an enforcement action
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson; U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
events.summary: The SEC Staff informed Ericsson that it had concluded its investigation concerning matters in the 2019 Iraq internal-investigation report and did not intend, based on the information then available, to recommend an enforcement action against Ericsson.

events.type: Securities class-action litigation concerning anti-corruption disclosures and Iraq conduct
events.jurisdiction: United States — Eastern District of New York and Second Circuit
events.parties: Ericsson and certain officers; purchasers of Ericsson ADS
events.summary: A putative class action alleged securities-law violations tied principally to Ericsson's compliance and anti-corruption disclosures and Iraq conduct; the district court dismissed it with prejudice on May 24, 2023, and the Second Circuit affirmed the dismissal on September 3, 2024.

output.assessment: The entity is identified as Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson, the Swedish parent company in the Ericsson group; Ericsson's official sources identify Stockholm, Sweden as its global headquarters and the homepage identifies the Ericsson group (https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts, https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts/ericsson-worldwide/sweden, https://www.ericsson.com/en). Risk is high because the parent company faced a 2019 multi-country FCPA DPA and SEC settlement and then a 2023 guilty-plea resolution for breaching the DPA. The latest opened company filing states that the SEC did not intend to recommend an enforcement action in the Iraq-related inquiry, but that Ericsson continued cooperating with an ongoing DOJ investigation whose scope and duration remained uncertain; no later outcome was verified from a page opened in this run.
missing_fields: Post-2024 outcome of the DOJ Iraq-related investigation
Any later bribery or corruption enforcement after the latest opened source dated 2024-10-15
